body:
# Description

Fixes #5887.

`electrolyte_diffusivity_Ai2020` uses the Valoen and Reimers (2005) correlation, `D = 10^(-4.43 - 54 / (T - 229 - 5e-3 c) - 0.22e-3 c)`, which gives cm2/s. It returned that value as m2/s, so the electrolyte diffusivity was 1e4 times too large: 3.2e-6 m2/s at 1000 mol/m3 and 298.15 K, against about 3e-10 m2/s for a typical LiPF6 carbonate electrolyte. `Xu2019.electrolyte_diffusivity_Valoen2005` implements the same fit and multiplies by 1e-4. The exponent here was -8.43, which includes that factor, until #3635 changed it to -4.43 without a stated reason.

The function now multiplies by 1e-4, as Xu2019 does, and its docstring says it returns the electrolyte diffusivity in m2/s (it said "Solid diffusivity").

Effect on a 1C DFN discharge with Ai2020 (3600 s):

| | final voltage | c_e range at the end |
|---|---|---|
| main | 3.3950 V | 1000.0 to 1000.1 mol/m3 |
| this PR | 3.3416 V | 668.4 to 1683.4 mol/m3 |

Thanks @EthanJamesLew for the report.

## Type of change

Bug fix, with an entry under `## Bug fixes` in CHANGELOG.md.

# Important checks:

- [x] No style issues: ruff 0.16.10 format and check, and comment-slop, pass on the changed files
- [x] Tests added that prove fix is effective: `TestAi2020.test_electrolyte_diffusivity` compares Ai2020 with Xu2019 (same fit) at three concentrations and temperatures with `rtol=1e-12`, and checks the value at 1000 mol/m3 and 298.15 K with a relative tolerance. It fails on main and passes with the fix. The existing `test_functions` uses `abs=1e-4`, which cannot see an error in a value of order 1e-10, so I added a separate test.
- [ ] All tests pass: every test file that uses Ai2020 passes locally (395 passed, 7 skipped), as do the particle cracking, swelling and loss of active material integration tests that use it (39 passed). I have not run the full `nox -s tests`, so I am relying on CI for the rest.
- [ ] The documentation builds: not run locally, no docs changes
- [x] Code is commented for hard-to-understand areas

commits.messageBody:
electrolyte_diffusivity_Ai2020 uses the Valoen and Reimers (2005) fit, which
gives cm2/s, but returned it as m2/s, so the electrolyte diffusivity was 1e4
times too large (3.2e-6 m2/s at 1000 mol/m3 and 298 K) and a DFN discharge had
almost no electrolyte concentration gradient. Multiply by 1e-4, as
Xu2019.electrolyte_diffusivity_Valoen2005 does for the same fit, and test
the result against Xu2019 with a relative tolerance.

Fixes #5887

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: fix: convert Ai2020 electrolyte diffusivity from cm2/s to m2/s

commits.messageBody:
- Check every Ai2020 function value with rel=1e-3 (abs=0), and add the
  electrolyte diffusivity and conductivity to the table, so values of order
  1e-20 to 1e-10 are actually checked. Drop the fixed-value check that this
  now covers.
- Cite Valoen and Reimers (2005) eqn 14 for the electrolyte diffusivity, and
  give electrolyte_conductivity_Ai2020 parameter units and the right Returns
  description.
- Link the issue as well as the PR in the CHANGELOG entry.
